covers.title: Opening title
covers.text: The file starts with the title company and the escrow officer opening title on the property under contract.

covers.title: The title commitment
covers.text: A commitment showing ownership interests, liens, encumbrances or defects goes to you for review before closing.

covers.title: Clearing the title
covers.text: The title agent works with the sellers to remove any title defects so the property closes on clear title.

covers.title: The owner's policy
covers.text: At closing you receive a title insurance policy that protects you for as long as you own the property.

questions.a: It is purchased at the time of the transaction, and it insures against events that occurred in the past history of the property.

questions.q: How long does the owner's policy last?
questions.a: The owner's policy protects the new owner for as long as the buyer owns the property.

services.title: Title Insurance
services.text: Title insurance protects owners and lenders against financial loss from liens, encumbrances or other defects in the title of the property, except those listed as exclusions in the policy.
services.lead: Anytime a property is sold or financed, there are public records of the transaction. There are also records that may affect the ownership of a property, such as liens, judgements, levies and encumbrances. Title insurance protects owners and lenders against financial loss from those defects, except the ones the policy lists as exclusions.
services.imageAlt: Two people signing documents across a desk

covers.title: Liens and judgements
covers.text: Financial loss from liens, judgements, levies and encumbrances recorded against the property.

covers.title: Defects in the title
covers.text: Other defects in the title of the property, apart from those listed as exclusions in the policy.

covers.title: The owner's policy
covers.text: Protects the new owner for as long as the buyer owns the property.

covers.title: The lender's policy
covers.text: Insures the lender's interest in the property for as long as the loan is outstanding.

questions.q: What does title insurance actually insure against?
questions.a: It insures against events that occurred in the past history of the property, rather than against something that might happen later.

questions.q: Why are there two policies at a closing?
questions.a: The owner's policy covers the buyer's ownership, and the lender's policy separately insures the lender's interest for as long as the loan is outstanding.

services.title: Title Search and Examination
services.text: The title agent searches title data from previous transactions and public records to determine the title history of the property, then issues a commitment on what that search found.
services.lead: Before anything can close, somebody has to read the property's history. Our title agents go through title data information from previous transactions and public records to determine the title history of the property.

team.name: Maria DeForest
team.bio: As President for Envision Title, Maria DeForest has over a decade of experience in the title industry. Maria's number one priority is to provide the highest standard of customer service. She is knowledgeable in all aspects of title insurance and related services, as well as escrow procedures. She has put together an amazing team that works efficiently together to provide an awesome title experience for the client. Over the years, Maria's greatest pride and successes have come from creating and maintaining dedicated relationships with the people she works with, her partners in the industry and the clients she strives to serve with excellence. Maria enjoys spending time with her friends and family, whether it be traveling or just hanging out at home.
team.imageAlt: Maria DeForest, President of Envision Title

team.name: Lisa Helmbrecht
team.bio: Lisa Helmbrecht has over 43 years of experience in the title industry. Her passion is helping people. She can close residential real estate as well as commercial. Lisa loves spending her time off cooking, sewing, vacationing and most importantly spending time with her very large family.

team.name: Julie Gonzalez
team.bio: Julie has over 13 years of experience in the title industry, having started her career as a receptionist and working her way through every role to become an Escrow Officer. Her well-rounded background gives her a deep understanding of the closing process from start to finish. As a bilingual professional, Julie is able to communicate clearly with a diverse range of clients, helping ensure a smooth and confident closing experience. She especially enjoys closing day and finds great joy in assisting first-time homebuyers. Outside of work, Julie enjoys spending weekends with her husband watching movies and cooking together. She also loves spending time with her grandbaby and shopping with her daughters and mom.

team.name: Melissa Barahona
team.bio: Melissa began her career in the title industry at Envision Title as a receptionist, where she quickly developed a strong interest in the work and a desire to learn more. With a year of industry experience, her curiosity and dedication led her into her current role as an Escrow Assistant, a position she truly enjoys. As a bilingual professional, she is able to communicate clearly and effectively with a diverse range of clients, helping ensure a smooth and confident closing experience. She is always eager to continue learning and growing within the industry. Outside of work, she enjoys starting her mornings with a good cup of coffee, running and working out, spending time outdoors, reading, and making meaningful memories with her family.

faqs.a: Anytime a property is sold or financed, there are public records of the transaction. There are also records that may affect the ownership of a property, such as liens, judgements, levies and encumbrances. Title insurance protects owners and lenders against financial loss from liens, encumbrances or other defects in the title of the property, except those listed as exclusions in the policy.

faqs.q: When is it purchased, and what does it cover?
faqs.a: Title insurance is purchased at the time of the transaction and insures against events that occurred in the past history of the property.

faqs.q: How long does each policy last?
faqs.a: The owner's policy protects the new owner for as long as the buyer owns the property, and a lender's policy insures the lender's interest in the property for as long as the loan is outstanding.

faqs.q: How does the closing process start?
faqs.a: The process starts with the title company and escrow officer opening title. The title agent then searches the property's title data and public records to determine its title history.

faqs.q: What happens if the search finds a problem?
faqs.a: The title agent works with the sellers to remove any title defects in order to get a clear title, then provides a title insurance policy that protects the client from issues that might not have been known or determinable at the time of the transaction.
